items.event_time_ist: Oct 21, 2026 — Wednesday morning (Lusail, Qatar; ~midday CEST Paris)
items.summary: From Lusail, Qatar, on Wednesday morning, Oct 21, Emmanuel Macron vowed there would be no repeat of last weekend's disorder: 'les gens qui veulent faire le désordre dans les centres-villes samedi prochain seront empêchés de faire du désordre' — those seeking disorder in city centres next Saturday (Oct 24) will be stopped. He announced a Thursday, Oct 22 morning meeting with all intelligence services, PM Lecornu and the concerned ministers for a detailed account of exactly what happened on Oct 17. He dismissed 'visible foreign interference' in the events themselves but said there had been 'foreign manipulation of information' afterwards. He also defended maintaining his Gulf tour ('il ne doit pas y avoir de fébrilité') and cited diesel and 2 TWh/month of LNG secured from Qatar for the winter. Corroborated by Boursorama/TF1 Info coverage of the same Doha press remarks.
items.title: Oct 21: Macron warns would-be rioters from Qatar — Thursday intel meeting on Oct 17 failures

items.event_time_ist: Oct 21, 2026 — Wednesday morning (~09:14 GMT / 2:44 PM IST)
items.summary: France's benchmark 10-year OAT yield touched 5.002% on Wednesday morning, Oct 21 — the first print at or above 5% since July 2002, a 24-year high. The premium over German Bunds was around 157bp, nearing levels last seen in 2011. Markets are worried the unrest will complicate the government's efforts to repair strained public finances (€54bn savings targeted in the 2027 budget) with a presidential election looming. Corroborated by Metapress's same-day coverage.
items.title: Oct 21: French 10-year bond yield hits 5%, first time since 2002

items.summary: Carrefour, Europe's largest food retailer, cut its targets for operating profit margin growth on Tuesday, Oct 20, because of the riots — the first major corporate earnings casualty of the unrest. Corroborated by Orbit Post's timeline of the market fallout.
items.title: Oct 20: Carrefour cuts margin targets, blaming the riots
